newsitem.title: USA: Christopher to meet Annan in New York.
newsitem.headline: Christopher to meet Annan in New York.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher, who is to leave office soon, will meet new U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan in New York on Tuesday, the State Department said on Monday.
The talks are expected to set the tone for a visit by Annan to Washington, possibly later this month, and for U.S. ties with the new U.N. chief.

Issues on the agenda include the U.S. debt of more than $1 billion in back dues to the world body, and the U.S. desire to see the United Nations steamlined. U.S. officials believed Annan's predecessor Boutros Boutros-Ghali did not do enough to cut costs and make the U.N. bureaucracy more efficient.

Even though the United States forced Boutros-Ghali's ouster and engineered his replacement with its preferred candidate -- Annan -- some congressmen and senators have resisted commiting themselves to approve paying the back dues until they are convinced Annan is serious about reform.
Among those is Republican Sen. Jesse Helms of North Carolina, chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, who has invited Annan to tea when he visits Washington.

Christopher is due to end his four-year term as secretary of state on or about Jan. 20 -- when President Bill Clinton is to be sworn in for a second term. Christopher is to be replaced by Madeleine Albright, who has been U.N. ambassador.
